items.text: AMEND (T) AND RECOMMIT TO WOMEN'S ISSUES

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to permitting expecting and
new mothers' access to their doulas and requiring maternal health care
facilities provide a directory of available doulas
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5992

SPONSOR: PERSAUD
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public health law, in relation to permitting expect-
ing and new mothers' access to their doulas and requiring maternal
health care facilities provide a directory of available doulas

 
PURPOSE:

Allows pregnant persons to designate a doula to have full access to
themselves and their newborn infant throughout a maternal health facili-
ty.

Requires all maternal health facilities to include a directory of prac-
ticing doulas on their website, to be posted throughout the facilities
and translated in the six most common languages in the region.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the public health law by adding a new section that
requires maternal health facilities to allow a pregnant person and their
newborn infant full access to their designated doula throughout the
facility.

Section 2 requires all maternal health care facilities to post a direc-
tory of practicing doulas on their websites and in their facilities, to
be translated in the six most common languages in the region.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Doulas provide non-clinical evidence-based practices that have been
proven to generate healthier outcomes for both a birthing person and
their child. They have proven to be an effective strategy in addressing
racial disparities in maternal healthcare by reducing severe maternal
morbidity and mortality. Yet, lack of awareness and access to doula
services contribute to underuse of this important resource.

A 2021 report by the NYC Department of Health found that doulas face
barriers to providing services in hospital settings, such as requests to
prove their training and/or certification (neither of which are required
in New York State) and inability to see their clients postpartum. Ensur-
ing pregnant persons and their child have access to their designated
doula throughout maternal health facilities has been shown to mitigate
stressors that influence birth outcomes.

The presence of a doula can empower a pregnant person to make informed
decisions and facilitate communication with healthcare providers.  They
also provide support and peace of mind in caring for the birthing
person's child once they are born. Providing a directory of doulas
allows maternal health facilities to mitigate disparities in maternal
healthcare by raising awareness of this service and making it more wide-
ly accessible.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPACT ON THE STATE:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 24 Chapter 550
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 5992-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend the public health law, in relation to permitting
        expecting and new mothers' access to their doulas"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This legislation would allow patients admitted to  a  maternal  health
care  facility for delivery or post-delivery inpatient care to designate
and have full access to a doula throughout the course of care.
 
  I fully support this legislation, which aims to expand access to doula
care for pregnant women. Doulas can advocate for a patient, as  well  as
provide   physical,  emotional,  and  informational  support,  typically
resulting in positive outcomes. However, changes are necessary to ensure
maternal health care facilities can  regulate  access  if  necessary  to
protect the safety of the patient or health care team, such as during an
emergency or when infection control measures are necessary.
 
  I have reached an agreement with the Legislature to enact these chang-
es.  On the basis of that agreement, I am pleased to sign this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______
